summary: Coordination umbrella for the 1.3.0 cross-platform validation day. Collects every fix blocked on a real build or on hardware: MPI-387 (Windows SAC laptop, 8 items in one install plus the transition update), MPI-370 (rented Mac, depth-model install - absence of the requirementsDrop line is the failure signal), MPI-198 (Linux, LOCAL engine plus subfoldered LoRA, which no Pod can provide), MPI-369 (build-time artifact-name and delta checks at the cut) and MPI-334 (in-app update prompt, first live test against a real release). Deliberately excludes MPI-385, MPI-387 gap 4, MPI-376, MPI-380 and MPI-291, each with a stated reason, so nothing is missed by accident. Placed top of To do; brief.md carries the ordered procedure and checklist.md is the tickable ledger for handoffs.

Two gaps closed after a coverage audit against the doing column. (1) NEW section A item 0: publish-runtime.sh promote. MPI-398's Pod fix is on the R2 dev channel only - wrapper 0.2.40, stable still 0.2.38 - and a dev app run boots dev, so the omission is INVISIBLE locally while released users boot stable and lose the fix entirely, keeping the 125s du behaviour on every Pod they open. mpi-release never auto-promotes by design, same class as git push, so it is a human step that breaks nothing locally when skipped - hence the most expensive item on the card to forget. (2) MPI-249 named as co-owner on the macOS and Linux smoke lines plus one artifact line each; it was doing this card's work while sitting unattributed in todo.

Picked up at the 1.3.0 cut. Section A is DONE and verified (evidence on MPI-369): CI run 30559394491 green on all three legs, 6 artifacts in D:CubricStudioVisionBuilds1.3.0 and integrity-tested, update-bundle root CubricVision-v1.3.0-update-only on all three, frozen Windows update asset name intact, every manifest reads from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0, counts 6418/6563/6383 (+56/+58/+58), baselines restamped (36f972cf). Card was sitting in todo while its own section A was being worked. Two sequencing findings recorded on checklist.md: the in-app update items cannot run before gh release create because the check hits releases/latest, and this dev PC cannot stand in for the SAC laptop because git resolves here. Machine order set by the user: dev PC first as a cheap early-fail filter, then Windows laptop, then Linux, Mac last because it bills hourly.
